newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Irish minister sees regional easing of UK beef ban.
newsitem.headline: Irish minister sees regional easing of UK beef ban.

text.p: Irish agriculture minister Ivan Yates said on Monday that most European Union member states favoured a regional approach to easing a worldwide ban on British beef exports.

Northern Irish herds would be the first to benefit under the plan which involves exempting herds which have been tracked from birth and have not been fed contaminated meat and bone meal, which is blamed for causing mad cow disease.
"I detected a willingness amongst virtually all member states to pursue a regional...lifting of the ban," Yates told reporters before a meeting of EU farm ministers.
He said that the main obstacle was the delay of the British government in presenting a specific proposal.
"I think there is some frustration," Yates said, adding it was up to the British authorities to make the next move.

Asked when this might be, Yates said, "It seems to me likely that this work is more likely to reach fruition sooner rather than later," noting the British government's dependence on Northern Irish MPs in the UK parliament.

Their vote could be crucial on Monday night when the parliament votes on an opposition Labour call to censure farm minister Douglas Hogg for his handling of the crisis caused by last year's government admission that mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), could be transmitted to humans.
The admission caused consumer panic across Europe and led to a collapse in beef prices. The EU responded by banning British beef exports.
Yates said he thought it was possible to restrict animal movements between Northern Ireland and the United Kingdom which would allow a phased lifting of the ban.

"We are spending millions of pounds policing the border and we feel that the incidence of BSE in Northern Ireland is significantly at variance with that in England that it would justify such an approach," he said.
